6                 IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT                    
7                     FOR THE DISTRICT OF ARIZONA                        

8                                                                        

9   Sam Alich,                         No. CV-22-01717-PHX-MTL           

10              Plaintiff,              ORDER                             

11   v.                                                                   

12   Opendoor Technologies Incorporated, et al.,                          

13              Defendants.                                               
14                                                                        
15        On February 28, 2024, the Court issued its Order dismissing Plaintiffs’ Consolidated 
16   Amended Complaint with leave to amend. (Doc. 86.) Among other things, the Court found 
17   that Plaintiffs’ claim brought pursuant to Section 11 of the Securities Act of 1933 failed 
18   because “Defendants have established negative causation because they have demonstrated 
19   that Plaintiffs do not allege a corrective disclosure or any other indication of loss causation 
20   in their Consolidated Amended Complaint.” (Id. at 31.) It also found that Plaintiffs had not 
21   alleged a claim under Section 15 of the Securities Act of 1933 because they did not allege 
22   a primary violation of Section 11. (Id. at 31-32.)                   
23        Plaintiffs filed their Motion for Reconsideration, which Defendants oppose. (Docs. 
24   87, 89.) After considering the parties’ briefing, relevant authorities, and Local Rule of Civil 
25   Procedure  7.2(g),  the  Court  finds  that  reconsideration  is  warranted  and  will  grant 
26   the Motion.                                                          
27        To establish negative causation, Defendants must “prove” that Plaintiffs’ claimed 
28   losses  are  “not  attributable  to  the  alleged  misrepresentation  .  .  .  in  the  registration 
1   statement.” Hildes v. Arthur Andersen LLP, 734 F.3d 854, 860 (9th Cir. 2013) (cleaned 
2   up). The issue is typically reserved for summary judgment, except for when negative 
3   causation is apparent from the face of the complaint. Brown v. Ambow Educ. Holding Ltd., 
4   No. CV 12-5062 PSG (AJWx), 2014 WL 523166, at *16 (C.D. Cal. Feb. 6, 2014). But that 
5   exception  requires  more  than  a  plaintiff’s  failure  to  allege  loss  causation.  See  In  re 
6   Facebook, Inc. IPO Sec. & Derivative Litig., 986 F. Supp. 2d 487, 522-23 (S.D.N.Y. 2013). 
7   Here, the Court is unable to find negative causation from the face of the Consolidated 
8   Amended Complaint, and even if it were, Plaintiffs would be provided leave to amend. 
9   This  issue,  thus,  is  better  reserved  for  summary  judgment.  See  Mallen  v.  Alphatec 
10   Holdings, Inc., 861 F. Supp. 2d 1111, 1131, aff’d, 607 F. App’x 694 (9th Cir. 2015). 
11        Additionally,  the  Court  finds  that  Defendants’  misleading  statement—that 
12   Opendoor’s algorithm “can dynamically adjust to leading market indicators and react to 
13   real-time macro- and micro-economic conditions”—touches upon the alleged reasons for 
14   Plaintiffs’ claimed losses. Hildes, 734 F.3d at 861 (applying the rule that “overcoming a 
15   negative causation defense requires merely that the misrepresentation touches upon the 
16   reasons for an investment’s decline in value”) (cleaned up). The Court therefore finds that 
17   Plaintiffs have adequately alleged a claim under Section 11.         
18        The Court must also revisit its conclusion that Plaintiffs have not pleaded a violation 
19   of Section 15. “To state a claim under Section 15, a plaintiff must show that: (1) there is a 
20   primary  violation  of  the  Securities  Act;  and  (2)  the  defendant  directly  or  indirectly 
21   controlled the person or entity liable for the primary violation.” Pino v. Cardone Cap., 
22   LLC, 55 F.4th 1253, 1257 (9th Cir. 2022) (cleaned up). As stated, the Court finds that 
23   Plaintiffs have pleaded a primary violation of Section 11.  The Court also finds that 
24   Plaintiffs have adequately alleged that the Securities Act Individual Defendants “controlled 
25   the person or entity liable for the primary violation.”* Id.; (see Doc. 39 ¶¶ 362-74, 496-99.) 
26   Therefore, Plaintiffs have stated a claim under Section 15.          
27                                                                        
    * The Securities Act Individual Defendants include Defendants Eric Wu, Carrie Wheeler, 
28   Adam Bain, Cipora Herman, Pueo Keffer, Glenn Solomon, Jason Kilar, Jonathan Jaffe, 
    Chamath Palihapitiya, Steven Trieu, Ian Osborne, and David Spillane. (Doc. 39 ¶¶ 362-74.) 
 1          Accordingly, 
2          IT IS ORDERED that Plaintiffs’ Motion for Reconsideration (Doc. 87) is granted. 
3          IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that the Court’s February 28, 2024 Order (Doc. 86) 
4||    is vacated in part and amended as follows only: 
5          1.     Plaintiffs have adequately alleged a claim under Section 11 of the Securities 
6||    Act of 1933 against all Defendants with respect to Defendants’ statement that Opendoor’s 
      algorithm  “can  dynamically  adjust  to  leading  market  indicators  and  react to  real-time 
8 ||  macro- and micro-economic conditions.” 
9          2.     Plaintiffs have adequately alleged a claim under Section 15 of the Securities 
10 ||  Act of 1933 against the Securities Act Individual Defendants with respect to Defendants’ 
11 ||  same statement. 
12          IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that the Court’s negative causation analysis in its 
13 ||  February 28, 2024 Order (Doc. 86 at 30-31) shall not constitute the law of the case and will 
      not bind the Court in any future motion to dismiss or other dispositive motion. 
15          IT IS FINALLY ORDERED that the stay on Plaintiffs’ deadline to file a second 
16 ||  amended complaint is lifted. If Plaintiffs choose to file a second amended complaint, they 
  ||  must do so no later than Friday, May 31, 2024. 
18          Dated this 14th day of May, 2024. 
19 
                                     Mi Charl T.  Siburde 
                                                 Michael  T. Liburdi 
22                                            United  States District Judge
